D013-D008_h001.question: It’s been about five months now, and honestly, I just feel… flat. Like a deflated balloon. Getting out of bed is a monumental effort. At work, I hardly say a word to customers, just point them in the right direction. My boss has noticed, and I’m definitely not hitting my sales targets. I used to be pretty quick on my feet, but now, when someone asks me something, it’s like my brain hit a brick wall. The words just won't come out. I just feel so useless, like I’m not contributing anything to anyone. I’ve started thinking about ways to just… end it. Not in any specific way, just how easy it would be to not be here anymore. Sometimes, a few times over the past couple of weeks, I feel a bit more energetic, almost restless, and I just start talking really fast, feeling like I can conquer anything, but it’s always fleeting. It’s mostly just this heavy sadness.
D013-D008_h001.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D013-D008_h001.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D013-D008_h002.question:
"It's been a rough five months, Doc. I just feel… empty. Like there’s a big hollow space where my feelings used to be. Sometimes it gets so bad, I just can’t sit still, I’ll pace around the house for hours, twisting my hands. My ex-wife, she says I’m just overthinking everything, but I can’t shake this feeling that I’ve messed everything up. I keep replaying old mistakes, feeling guilty about things that probably don’t even matter anymore.

I find myself thinking, 'What’s the point?' more and more. Not like I’d ever do anything, but just a quiet wish that I wouldn’t wake up. It’s hard to focus on work; my mind just drifts, and honestly, the thought of crawling into tight attics or damp crawl spaces just drains me entirely. Lately, though, there are these other times. I get this sudden burst of energy, almost like I’m buzzing with it, and I feel like I could conquer anything. But then it just… fades, and I’m back to feeling nothing again. It’s like a switch flips, and I’m just waiting for the next slump."
D013-D008_h002.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D013-D008_h002.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D013-D008_h003.question: It's been about five months now, and honestly, I just feel… flat. Everything feels muted, like I’m watching my life through a pane of thick glass. I’m married, I have a good job as a fund manager, but I just can't connect to any of it. My wife tries, but I just feel numb to everything. It’s hard to sit still; I find myself constantly pacing the office, wringing my hands, sometimes even picking at my cuticles without realizing it. And the guilt… it’s overwhelming. I know it sounds crazy, but I’m convinced the market dip last quarter was my fault, that I somehow single-handedly ruined clients' portfolios, even though all the numbers say otherwise. Sometimes, I’ll be walking near a busy street and this terrifying urge to just… step out… flashes through my mind. I don't want to act on it, but the thought alone is enough to shake me. It’s making it impossible to focus on work or anything else.

A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder

D013-D008_h004.question:
"It's been... I guess about five months now," I start, my voice feeling a bit heavy, like my tongue is moving through molasses. "Everything just feels… *dark*. Not just sad, you know? But this deep-seated gloom that just won't lift. Even talking feels like too much effort sometimes, like my thoughts are stuck in a slow-motion replay."

I shift in my seat, a wave of discomfort washing over me. "And the guilt… It’s ridiculous. Like, if a flight gets delayed twenty minutes, I'll replay every single transmission, convinced I could've done something, even if it was totally out of my control. I feel like I'm letting everyone down, my wife, my team… everyone. Sometimes, honestly, I just wish I wouldn't wake up. Not in a 'killing myself' kind of way, just… to be done with it all. To not feel this anymore."

"There have been these other moments, though," I continue, almost reluctantly. "Flashes, really. Short bursts where I feel… a rush. Like I could conquer anything, and my mind races with ideas, needing less sleep and talking a mile a minute. My wife says I get really intense, sometimes even irritable, during those times. But then it just… stops, and I'm back here, in the grey. It’s making it really hard to focus at work, and with everything going on, I just don’t know what to do."
D013-D008_h004.options:
A. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    B. Major Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar I Disorder
    D. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
D013-D008_h004.answer: B & C. Major Depressive Disorder & Bipolar I Disorder

D013-D008_h006.question:

And the impulses… sometimes I’ll be walking near a busy street and just have this flash, this urge to just run into traffic, or if I’m on a high floor, to just jump. It’s fleeting, and I don’t have a plan, but it scares me. But then other times, I feel this surge of energy, like I could work for days without needing rest.
